newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher in lackluster trading.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher in lackluster trading.

text.p: COMEX copper settled slightly higher after after a dull session with a sharp drop in LME stocks failing to prod any significant moves though it helped the London contract close above $1,900 a tonne.
LME stocks fell 9,925 tonnes to 229,575 tonnes, with some brokers suggesting that much of the material left European warehouses destined for China.
"I think the stock drop does reflect a global market still in deficit," said John Gross of The Copper Journal.
Trading volumes on COMEX were thin as many players were out of the market as they readied for LME Week in London starting over the weekend.
December COMEX settled 0.30 cent firmer at 89.15 cents, traded narrowly between 89.80 to 88.95 cents. Spot October went out 0.50 cent firmer.
Over the week COMEX has remained in backwardation with spot higher than forward prices, while the LME maintained its recently established albeit slim contango.
On the U.S. physical market, merchants said scrap was still tight as the volumes flowing into yards was low for this time of year.
